title: throughput-regression-continuous-batching-user-scratchpad-4
content:
Context:
- Spike in per-cluster throughput regression observed starting ~2026-02-25 18:00 UTC. Affected: hosted-production cluster eu-west-1-gpu-pool-3 (pools behind routing policy 'latency-first').
- Regression = ~30% drop in tokens/s on steady-state load (small short requests mix).
- Initial suspicion: continuous batching change + per-route policy tweak rolled last week (PR #1234).

Symptoms / Metrics observed:
- Baseline (2026-02-20): 120k tokens/s steady on 8 nodes (avg batch size ~8, avg latency 85ms).
- After incident: 80k tokens/s, avg batch size dropped to ~3, avg latency slightly improved for single requests but tail latency worse under load (p95 up by 40ms).
- KV cache hit ratio decreased from 72% -> 31% (logs from cache-metrics export).
- Batching backlog length metric (batcher.queue_len) shows fewer items accumulating before flush.
- GPU utilization per worker decreased by ~15% (consistent with smaller batches).

Timeline (quick):
- 2026-02-24 11:12 UTC: Canary of batch-optimizations v2 merged (PR #1228) to canary pool.
- 2026-02-24 17:45 UTC: Routing policy change (per-route) to 'latency-first' for some customers (PR #1234) -> rollout 100% by 2026-02-25 09:00 UTC.
- 2026-02-25 18:00 UTC: Ops alerted for sustained throughput drop.

Commands / checks I ran (notes + outputs paraphrased):
1) Reproduced simple load locally against canary: wrk -t8 -c200 -d60s --lua=small-requests.lua -> observed batch sizes small, throughput low.
2) Check batcher config via admin endpoint: curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://admin.eu/cluster/config/batcher | jq
   -> returned: {"max_batch_tokens":256, "max_batch_items":16, "max_latency_ms":4}  # suspiciously low max_latency_ms
3) kubectl logs batcher-0 -n serving | tail -n 200
   -> repeating messages: [batcher] flushed small batch (len=2) due to latency budget exceeded (elapsed_ms=4)
4) cache debug: curl admin/metrics | grep kvcache_hit
   -> kvcache_hit_count: 43123 (down), kvcache_miss_count: 94023 (up)
5) Checked recent config commits: git log --since="2026-02-20" -- author:platform -> includes PR #1234 that changed per-route policy mapping and lowered default max_latency_ms for latency-first customers.

Error snippets / logs of interest:
- [2026-02-25T18:03:12Z] batcher.cpp: flush_small_batch(): reason=latency_budget_exceeded elapsed_ms=4 len=2
- [2026-02-25T18:03:12Z] kv_cache.cc: lookup_batch(): miss_count=18 keys=[...], client_route=route-xyz
- [2026-02-25T18:03:12Z] router.cpp: apply_policy(): policy=latency-first -> batching.max_latency_ms=4

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Per-route policy change to 'latency-first' set max_latency_ms too low (4ms) which causes early flush of batches, reducing effective batching and lowering throughput. Explains batch size drop and decrease in KV cache hits (less opportunity to reuse KV across adjacent requests).
2) Canary of batch-optimizations v2 interacts poorly with 'latency-first' (e.g., faster flush path triggers earlier eviction of KV entries / shorter KV lifetime).
3) A separate bug in the batcher that miscomputes elapsed_ms under certain timers when load pattern has many short requests; less likely because logs explicitly show config applied.

Immediate mitigations tried (and results):
- Increase max_latency_ms to 20ms for affected route (via admin patch) and watched throughput recover to ~112k tokens/s over 10 minutes. (temporary but confirms hypothesis #1).
- Rolled back per-route mapping for a small subset of customers -> throughput normalized for those routes.
- Reverted canary of batch-optimizations v2 on one node pool -> no measurable difference when policy still had low max_latency_ms.

Reproduction steps (short):
1) Apply policy 'latency-first' with max_latency_ms=4 to a route.
2) Run mixed small chat-style load (many short requests, steady QPS) using wrk script.
3) Observe avg batch size drop and tokens/s drop, check metrics above.

Notes on root cause indicators:
- The admin config surfaced the low max_latency_ms value; changing it reproduced/resolved the regression quickly.
- KV cache hit ratio falling is an expected side-effect of smaller batching.
- Routing policy change was rolled within a couple of days of the throughput regression window -> high confidence linking policy change to regression.

Next steps / action items:
- Short term (today): keep max_latency_ms bumped to 20ms for affected routes + monitor for p95 latency regressions. Add alert if tokens/s drops >10% for 15m. (Assigned: Ethan)
- Mid term: revert or adjust PR #1234 to set safer default for max_latency_ms (maybe 8-16ms range depending on workload). (Assigned: Priya/Lena)
- Longer term: add a canary test that runs mixed short-request workload when changing per-route batching policy. Add automated check that compares batch size and kv_cache hit ratio pre/post rollout. (Owner: eng-serving-runtime)
- Instrumentation: add per-route batch_size histogram and expose kv-cache effective window metric.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Does the 'latency-first' policy have other knobs we can tune to preserve batching (e.g., per-route min_batch_items)?
- Are there customers where increased max_latency_ms will lead to unacceptable p95 regressions? Need to contact a couple of affected accounts for opt-in testing.
- Confirm whether batch-optimizations v2 has code paths that shorten KV lifetime under certain flush conditions. Add unit tests.

Quick breadcrumbs for whoever picks this up:
- Admin patch that temporarily increased latency budget: admin://config/patches/patch-2026-02-26-14
- Related PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1228 (batch-optimizations-v2), github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1234 (routing policy defaults)
- JIRA: INF-4823 (Throughput regression — continuous batching / routing policy interaction)

Raw note (scratch) of commands I ran (copy-paste):
- wrk -t8 -c200 -d60s --lua=small-requests.lua http://canary.serving.local/v1/generate
- curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://admin.eu/cluster/config/batcher | jq
- kubectl -n serving logs -l app=batcher --tail=300 > /tmp/batcher-logs.txt
- curl https://admin.eu/metrics | grep kvcache_hit_count

If I get pulled off this, leave it with Ethan. I'll follow up on PR 1234 rollback and adding the canary test.

-- Priya
